Day 1
From Hotel: 25 min · 8 min → Wat Chedi Luang
1. Wat Chedi Luang
The great ruined chedi at the center of the Old City, begun in 1391 and once the tallest structure in the Lanna kingdom. At its peak the chedi stood over 80 meters; an earthquake in 1545 collapsed the upper third, leaving the dramatic broken profile that stands today.

Phrasing Road · Old City
12 min · 3 min → Wat Phra Singh
2. Wat Phra Singh
The principal royal temple of Chiang Mai, built in 1345 to house the ashes of King Kham Fu. The Wihan Lai Kham — a 14th-century pavilion — holds rare Lanna-style murals depicting northern Thai village life, among the finest surviving examples of Lanna painting.
Read more

Singharat Road · Old City
10 min · 5 min → Three Kings Monument
3. Three Kings Monument
A bronze monument depicting the three rulers who jointly chose this valley as the site for Chiang Mai in 1296 — King Mangrai of Lanna, King Ngam Muang of Phayao, and King Ramkhamhaeng of Sukhothai. The figures stand on a raised plinth in front of the Old City's civic buildings.
Read more
Open 24/7

Phra Pokklao Road · Old City
1 min · 2 min → Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Center
4. Chiang Mai City Arts & Cultural Center
Chiang Mai's foremost civic museum, housed in the 1924 former Provincial Hall directly opposite the Three Kings Monument. Fifteen themed rooms trace Lanna civilisation from origins through craft, religion, and folk life. Among the finest colonial civic structures in northern Thailand.
Read more

10 min · 4 min → Wat Chiang Man
5. Wat Chiang Man
The oldest temple in Chiang Mai, founded by King Mengrai in 1296 when he established the city. The compound contains two sacred Buddha images — the Crystal Buddha and the Phra Sila bas-relief — and a distinctive chedi rising from a ring of carved stone elephants.

Day 2
From Hotel: 2h 15min → Doi Inthanon National Park
1. Doi Inthanon National Park
Thailand's highest peak at 2,565 metres, 75 km southwest. The park spans cloud forest, twin Royal Chedis, and the Wachirathan and Siriphum waterfalls. The park holds the highest recorded bird diversity of any protected area in Thailand — over 390 species.

Day 3
From Hotel: 1h 38min → Elephant Nature Park
1. Elephant Nature Park
A rescue and rehabilitation sanctuary in the Mae Taeng valley. Operating since 1996, the park cares for elephants rescued from logging operations and tourist riding. Visitors walk alongside the herd in open pasture — no riding, no performance shows.

1h 6min → Chiang Dao Cave
2. Chiang Dao Cave
A series of limestone caverns at the base of Doi Chiang Dao, the third-highest peak in Thailand. Five chambers extend deep into the mountain — three lit by electricity, two traversable by lantern with a local guide only. Buddha images fill alcoves along the cave walls, some centuries old.
Read more

Amphoe Chiang Dao
1h 21min → Bua Tong Sticky Waterfall
3. Bua Tong Sticky Waterfall
A series of limestone terraces in Mae Taeng where calcium carbonate deposits coat the riverbed in a travertine-like layer — creating enough grip to walk directly up the cascades barefoot. Unlike any conventional waterfall, the falls can be climbed. The surrounding secondary forest is dense.

Day 4
From Hotel: 57 min → Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden
1. Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden
A 565-hectare botanical garden on Doi Suthep-Pui, opened in 1993 and named for Queen Sirikit. The garden holds the largest collection of wild orchids in Thailand, a glasshouse complex with eight climate-controlled zones, and a canopy walkway extending through protected highland forest at 1,050 meters.

11 min → Mae Sa Waterfall
2. Mae Sa Waterfall
A chain of ten tiered cascades in Mae Sa-Kog Ma Wildlife Sanctuary in Mae Rim, each level reachable by trail through dense forest. The falls run year-round; peak volume is September and October. The reserve is protected temperate forest at 900 meters — notably cooler than the city below.

1h 8min → Doi Suthep
3. Doi Suthep
The hilltop temple at 1,073 meters on Doi Suthep mountain, founded in 1383 after a white elephant chose the site. The compound centers on a gilded copper-plated chedi visible from across the city. The staircase of 309 Naga-flanked steps leads to panoramic views over the entire valley.

Day 5
From Hotel: 19 min · 4 min → Tha Phae Gate
1. Tha Phae Gate
The eastern gate of Chiang Mai's 1296 walled city. The sandstone archway at the end of Tha Phae Road flanks an intact moat wall — the most complete surviving section of the original Lanna fortification. The gate name recalls the teak rafts once floated down from the northern forests and unloaded at the pier below.
Read more
Open 24/7

23 min · 8 min → Mae Ping River Cruise
2. Mae Ping River Cruise
A longtail boat cruise on the Ping River — the principal waterway through Chiang Mai. Cruises pass orchid gardens, riverside temples, and traditional teak houses on the banks south of the Old City, offering a perspective on the city rarely available from the streets.

1. Ban Sao Nak
A Burmese-Lanna teak mansion in the heart of Lampang, built in 1895 for a local timber merchant and containing over 100 teak pillars. The interior holds antique ceramics, lacquerware, and period furniture from the teak trade era when Burmese merchants dominated the northern Thai timber industry.

2. Wat Phra That Lampang Luang
A 15th-century Lanna temple 18 km south of Lampang, regarded as one of the finest surviving examples of northern Thai wooden architecture in Southeast Asia. The wihan is open-sided with multi-tiered gilded gables; the inner sanctum houses a 7th-century Buddha image.

27 min → Kat Kong Ta
3. Kat Kong Ta
Lampang's 19th-century trading street along the Wang River, lined with Chinese-Burmese shophouses from the teak boom. The facades show carved wooden eaves and iron shutters; ground floors hold ceramics shops, coffee roasters, and local restaurants — among the best-preserved heritage streets in northern Thailand.

Local Tastes
Khao Soi
Northern Thailand's defining dish — a rich coconut curry broth with egg noodles, topped with crispy fried noodles and braised meat. The Lanna version runs heavier on spice paste and subtler on coconut sweetness than southern Thai curries.
Khao Soi Islam · Lamduan Faham
Sai Oua
Northern Thai sausage — coarsely ground pork packed with lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime leaf, dried chilli, and shrimp paste, grilled over charcoal. Sold by the link at market stalls across the city.
Somphet Market · Warorot Market

Day Trips by Train
Lamphun · 30 min
The ancient Hariphunchai kingdom capital — a small moated city with the Lamphun National Museum, Wat Chama Thewi, and a remarkably intact old town. One of the quietest and best-preserved historic cities in northern Thailand. Recommended by Lonely Planet and Rough Guides.
book at: Omio
Bangkok · 12 hr
The overnight sleeper train is one of Thailand's classic rail journeys — first-class sleeper carriages with folding berths and dining service, traversing the central plains and arriving at Bang Sue Grand Station. Recommended by Lonely Planet and The Guardian.
book at: Omio

Worth Knowing

The City in the Valley

Chiang Mai sits at 310 metres in the valley of the Ping River, ringed by highlands that reach 2,565 metres at Doi Inthanon — the same mountain reachable in under two hours from the Old City moat. That vertical difference of 2,255 metres in a single drive is one of the most dramatic elevation gradients accessible from any major Thai city.

The Bua Tong waterfall's grip comes from the mineral content of the springs feeding it. The water carries dissolved calcium carbonate; as it flows over limestone and meets the air, it precipitates as travertine — building up layer by layer into a rough coating. The same chemistry that builds stalagmites in caves is what lets bare feet walk straight up a waterfall.
